outcomes.name: Percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol
outcomes.definition: Every contributing registration declares this primary, so the OUTCOME limb passes. That is why an outcome-only screen passed this page and why it is not poolable on a different limb.
outcomes.measure_note: THE GENERATOR'S OWN IDIOM FOR ABSENCE. This topic publishes no estimate, so there is no measure it was expressed in. Not a borrowed value: sibling objects whose estimate was WITHDRAWN legitimately carry the withdrawn measure, which is a different case.
outcomes.definition_note: Registered endpoint definitions are recorded per trial on this object.

ldlc_pct_change.poolable_reason: ONE TRIAL HAS NO CONTROL ARM AND THE OTHER TWO ARE IN DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov 2026-08-18. NCT00477594 is an OPEN-LABEL EXTENSION whose two arms are BOTH mipomersen at different dosing intervals -- 200 mg weekly against 200 mg alternate weeks. It has no control and cannot contribute a controlled contrast at all; it is a within-drug dose question. That leaves two placebo-controlled trials, and they are in DIFFERENT POPULATIONS: NCT00607373 enrols HOMOZYGOUS familial hypercholesterolaemia, which is what this topic is titled for, and NCT00707746 enrols HIGH-RISK STATIN-INTOLERANT patients, which is not. FOR THE HoFH QUESTION THIS IS k=1. Mipomersen is correctly the experimental arm in all three, so the INTERVENTION limb passes; comparator and participants do not.

ldlc_pct_change.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that the trials are poor -- each is registered, randomised and reports its primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area -- only that the one this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials on it.

risk_of_bias_verdict: Not assessed. A risk-of-bias assessment grades the trials contributing to a result, and this page contributes none. Stated rather than left blank.
